title: The Loose-Parts Atelier
strapline: A studio of open-ended treasures — nothing tells the child what to make, so they make anything.
intent: Children combine, arrange and transform open-ended materials that can become anything, driving deep creative thinking.
Children make choices, plan and problem-solve with no fixed outcome — the materials pose the questions.
Children explore early maths and design through balancing, arranging, sorting, patterning and building.
Children develop concentration, agency and a sense of themselves as capable makers.
Children negotiate, share and build ideas together as their creations grow and change.
implementation: Curate a beautiful, well-organised collection — corks, buttons, rings, cogs, pebbles, tiles, keys, reels, shells — sorted in open trays.
Present it invitingly, like a studio, and let children lead entirely: there is no 'right' thing to make.
Resist naming what a creation 'is' — ask the child instead, and take their answer seriously.
Add a light table, mirror or frame some days to change how the materials look and invite new ideas.
Photograph creations before tidy-up so the fleeting, transient work is honoured.
Replenish and rotate the collection to keep it fresh, adding natural and reclaimed treasures.
Sit alongside as a fascinated observer, feeding in language for what children are doing, not directing it.
key_questions: Tell me about what you're making.
How did you decide to put those together?
How did you get it to balance like that?
What might you change or add next?

impact.text: Children combine and transform materials imaginatively.
Children make choices, plan and solve open-ended problems.
Children explore arranging, sorting, patterning and balancing.
Children concentrate deeply and sustain their own projects.
Children collaborate, sharing materials and building on ideas.
Children see themselves as capable, creative makers.

enhancements: A light table or mirror to transform how the loose parts look.
Frames, trays and hoops to arrange creations within.
Natural loose parts — cones, shells, seed pods, slices of branch.
Reclaimed treasures — cogs, corks, keys, tiles, offcuts.
A camera so children can photograph and keep their transient work.
A pairing with clay or dough as a base to build into.

playing_exploring: Children explore materials with no fixed purpose, following fascination.
They test, combine and rearrange endlessly.
active_learning: Children sustain their own projects with deep concentration.
They persist to make a creation balance or work as they intend.
creating_thinking: Children generate original ideas and represent them with materials.
They plan, adapt and problem-solve as their creation evolves.
